matching: Rules match one quote-aware simple command at a time. The canonical form is the command name followed by its expanded words joined by single spaces; for git the words start at the subcommand. Whitespace inside one word is folded to U+001F, so quoted text never forms a separate argument. match: command (default, skipped for pure-read commands) | pipeline (command names joined by |) | raw (full source text).

rules.reason: Recursive forced deletion is blocked, except for what the agent can make again: a known path strictly inside ~/.development-system/private/scratch or a temporary folder that holds no repository, or a build or cache folder that git ignores. For tracked paths use `git rm -r <path>` so the deletion stays reviewable and recoverable; for a worktree use `git worktree remove`; otherwise ask the owner.
Stop 1 (incremental spend): buying a domain or running Stripe in live mode costs money or moves it. Ask the owner first; test mode and reads stay allowed.
Disk formatting or raw device writes are blocked.
git reset --hard can destroy uncommitted work and is blocked.
git clean can destroy untracked work and is blocked; `git clean -n` (dry run) and `git clean -i` remain allowed.
Discarding worktree changes through Git (checkout --, checkout/switch --force, switch --discard-changes, restore) is blocked. `git checkout --ours/--theirs` and `git restore --staged` remain allowed.

Forced branch deletion is blocked unless every named branch is already merged into HEAD, develop, main or master (a squash merge leaves the branch unmerged for git: fetch and compare, or ask the owner).
Forced and mirror pushes are blocked by the global policy.
Piping downloaded code directly into a shell is blocked.
Only the operator grants test-file writes, by running `development-system allow-tests <dir>` in their own terminal. Ask them to run it; `development-system test-grants` lists active grants.

structuralRules.reason: Shell hook input contained no command; blocked closed.
Hook payload could not be inspected; blocked closed.

The command could not be parsed with confidence; blocked closed. A common cause is a program passed in single quotes that contains an apostrophe, or a bare backtick inside double quotes: put the program in a file or a quoted heredoc.
Command substitution or nested shell evaluation exceeds the inspected depth; blocked closed.
ANSI-C $'...' quoting outside single quotes can hide command text and is blocked. Use plain single or double quotes.
Indirect or evaluating parameter expansion (${!name}, zsh (e) flags) is blocked.
Glob qualifiers that execute code are blocked.
eval executes runtime-constructed code and is blocked.
Shell code built from a variable or substitution cannot be inspected and is blocked. Pass a literal script.
Running a shell script or interpreter program produced by process substitution or read from a device is blocked.
A shell or interpreter reading its commands from piped, inherited or non-literal standard input cannot be inspected and is blocked. Pass the program with -c/-e, a literal heredoc or a file.

The program to run comes from a variable or substitution the guard cannot read, so it is blocked. Write the program name out, or assign it a literal in the same command (`B=/path/to/tool; "$B" --version`).
This read command option executes other programs (rg --pre, sed e) and is blocked.

A destructive-capable program (rm, dd, mkfs, diskutil, gh, terraform, tofu, pulumi, kubectl, wrangler, vercel, or git) ran a subcommand that changes something, or one the policy does not classify, with a word the guard cannot read. Write the word out, or assign it a literal in the same command (`D=/path; rm -r "$D/x"`, `for n in 12 13; do gh pr close "$n"; done`). Subcommands that only read (`gh pr view "$n"`, `gh api "repos/$R/pulls"`, `vercel ls`, `kubectl get`) pass with any argument.

Creating or modifying automated test files or test runner configuration is blocked by the no-tests policy unless the operator granted that directory with `development-system allow-tests <dir>` in their own terminal; ask them for a grant. Deleting them is allowed.

Writing the guard's hook configuration (Claude Code settings, Codex hooks or config, including the project's .claude and .codex settings), the project's .git/config (its aliases run commands) the installed guard skill, the installed instructions (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/rules, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md: only installing a version changes them) or the operator's test-write grants is blocked; use the Development System guardrails commands, `git config`, or ask the user to make the edit.
Text shaped like `name[$(…)]` in an assignment, variable name, test or arithmetic runs the subscript as a command when evaluated and is blocked.
Git configuration that makes an ordinary command destructive (help.autocorrect, clean.requireForce=false, forced or deleting remote.*.push refspecs, remote.*.mirror) is blocked.
A PR merge needs --match-head-commit and a fresh merge pass from `development-system pr-review-status <pr> --gate` for that exact head.
